name: player_set_landed
args: no args (0 inline words)
evidence: Handler 0x80070868: actor[0].flags(+0xE4) = (flags & ~0x8) | 0x100. That is exactly the pair of writes the player motion code makes on landing (0x8003141C: clear airborne bit 0x8, set 0x100, then [0x800995D0] |= 0xA). Bit 0x100 is also tested at 0x80061828 (damage/hurt routine: if set, clear it, set airborne 0x8 again, play sfx 0xCB/0xCC at the player) and at 0x80068CE4/0x80068DB8 (facing-byte +0xF6 is not updated while it is set and [0x8007FD7E]==1). 91 uses in 63 dungeon scenes, nearly all in scene entry functions as 'a2 (actor 0, prop 1 = y); if y > 0xB4: 77' (player starts low on the screen -> treat as landed) or at the start of a pit/ledge trigger right after 'sys_81 7'. The meaning of 0x100 ('landed / hold') is inferred from the landing code, not observed; nothing run live (no reachable scene uses it).

name: clear_monster_fight_counts
args: no args (0 inline words); used only by library func_07FA
evidence: Handler 0x8007088C: memset(G+0x16C, 0, 128) and ctx+0x3C0 &= 0xC7. Op 0x86 start_battle (handler 0x800786E8) does G[0x16C + monster_index]++ on exactly that block, and library func_086B tests G[0x16C+index].b < 1 before letting a monster trigger an encounter, so the block is a per-monster 'fought' counter. Only user is library func_07FA (called 33x from scenes; in the two I read, scenes 0x29 and 0x7D, it comes right before a caption2 area-name call, e.g. scene 0x29 'x < 200 -> caption 3'), i.e. an area change resets the encounter counters. Never used in scene code directly (1 library use).

name: wait_event_image_ready
args: stack form pops one handle (the value 0xA5 returned); 0 or 1 inline words; 4 uses in 2 scenes (0x10, 0x38)
evidence: Core handler 0x8006F0D4 only calls the hook [0x8007F250]. In the ram6440 snapshot the hook is 0x8008A3CC (installed together with the 0xA5/0xA6 hooks 0x8008A16C/0x8008A284): it scans the 144 task slots for the 0xA5 task (function 0x800899E0) whose handle byte (+0x68) equals the argument and, if that task is still loading (state +4 != 4) or still fading (flags +0x5E bit 1), sets ctx+0x310 = 1 and rewinds ip (wait); no such task = no wait. Used right after a5/a6 with the same handle (then '8c 0x42'). Not run live (scenes 0x10/0x38 are not reachable early).

name: wait_palette_crossfade_done
args: operand low16 (or popped) = crossfade id returned in G0 by 0xA4; NEVER used in scene code
evidence: Handler 0x80071414 scans the 144 task slots for one whose function is 0x8005B130 with id byte +0x3A == arg and, if found, sets ctx+0x310 = 1 and rewinds ip. 0x8005B130 tasks are created only by op 0xA4 (handler 0x80071184, 3 references to the pointer, all in 0xA4/0x7A): it picks the first unused id (+0x3A), stores 8 halfwords and the update function blends 15-bit colours over N frames. So this is the per-id wait for 0xA4 (0x7B is the any-task wait for the 0xA0 tint tween 0x8004B618). Mechanism clear; both ops unused in scripts.

name: camera_pan_to_axiswise
args: like 0x83 (x in operand low16; word0 = y | speed<<16; word1 = low16: mode, high16: last param) but with 5 stack values; NEVER used in scene code
evidence: Handler 0x800784D8 calls the same pan routine 0x80077FD4 as 0x83, but passes a3 = (mode<<1)|1 instead of 0. a3 is stored in byte [0x8007FCB8] and read by the camera update at 0x800474D4..: bit0 set = axis-wise motion (all four speed fields get the same constant speed, 0x800783A0 branch, no atan2 direction vector), bit1 (the low bit of 'mode') chooses which axis is driven first - the code drives one axis until it reaches the target, flips bit1 (xori 2) and then does the other, so the camera travels an L-shaped path; bit2 = decelerating. 0x83 passes 0 = straight-line pan with eased speed. Mechanism read from code only (op unused).

name: bgm_start_loaded
args: operand low16 = N: 0 = start the loaded BGM at once, N > 0 = fade it in over N frames (0, 0x1e, 0x3c, 0x78, 0xf0 seen), N < 0 = variant at 0x8005A544; 0 inline words; 34 uses
evidence: LIVE (frame 6592, scene 0x16 start): handler 0x80078934 hit with N=0 right after 'play_bgm 0x8d5'; it allocates a task with function 0x8005A4C8 (+8 = N). Same frame the task ran and called 0x8001A5F8(sound manager 0x800964B4, sequence) = start the music sequence (bt: func_8005a4c8+0xd4 -> func_8001a5f8). The task first looks up the 0xBB loader task (type 0x800597B0) and waits until its state is >= 5 / 255 (load finished), then N>0: 0x8001A67C(mgr, seq, N, 0) which stores 30720/N as the per-tick volume step (mgr+0x16) and restarts the sequence; N==0: 0x8001A5F8; finally 0x80059F88(ctx+0x38C). If [0x8007F260] bit31 is set the handler instead resets the sound manager at once (0x8001A5F8 + 0x80059F88) and spawns nothing. So 0xBB = 'load music', 0x8D = 'start it (with fade-in)', 0x8E = fade out. Old name bgm_fade_in was right about N but missed the 'start' role.

name: get_zoom_tween_value
args: no args; result in G[0]; NEVER used in scene code
evidence: Handler 0x8007600C: finds the tween object with function 0x8004B5BC (the scalar tween created by 0x9C, which animates word 0x8007FC80, the layer scale factor 0x10000 = 1.0) and returns its current value (+0xC) in G[0]; if no tween is running it stores 0 (NOT the current scale). So it is 'current value of the running zoom tween'. Mechanism read from code; unused.

name: load_event_image
args: inline 2 words (stack 3): word0 = resource id (CD directory word 0x8F8..0x902 = 2296..2306), word1 = x | y<<16 screen offset (x 0x18/0x40/0x60/0x68, y usually 0); returns a handle in G[0]
evidence: Core handler 0x8006F07C calls hook [0x8007F248]; in the ram6440 snapshot that is 0x8008A16C, which creates the task 0x800899E0 (+0x30 = resource id, +0x44/+0x48 = x/y, handle counter [0x8007FD87] stored in +0x68, returned in G0). Task states: 0 read the CD directory word into a malloc'd buffer, 1 decompress_resource (entry 0 -> +0x10 table, entry 1 -> +0xC TIM), upload via 0x8001AB48/0x800563B4, 4 draw. The draw routine 0x80089DD4 reads the table as: header (w, h, tile 16x16), records kind 0 = row y, kind 1 = texture page word, kind 2 = n tiles of (x, clut, u, v), and emits GPU textured rectangles (cmd 0x64/0x66) with a brightness level. I decoded the resources myself: 0x8F8 (329x240, 129 tiles), 0x8FA (320x240, 256 tiles), 0x902 (216x240) rebuild into full-screen story illustrations (e.g. a crying blond boy; a blue-haired figure with raised arms), so this is a CG/event picture, not a sprite. Not run live (used in scenes 0xF 0x10 0x14 0x1F 0x38 0x123 only).

name: fade_event_image
args: stack only, 5 values popped (top first): handle, ignored, frames, level, ignored; typical '0,0x80,0x3c,0,L0' = fade in over 60 frames to level 0x80, '0,0,0x3c,0,L0' = fade to 0 (image removed)
evidence: Core handler 0x8006F0A8 -> hook 0x8008A284 (ram6440): finds the 0xA5 task by handle byte; if its state != 4 (still loading) it rewinds ip and bumps the wait counter, else stores frames (halfword) into +0x62, level (byte) into +0x64, sets +0x5E |= 3. The task's per-frame code (0x80089CA0) steps +0x60 up to +0x62 and interpolates the brightness (+0x66) from the old to the new level; level 0x80 = normal brightness; when it reaches 0 the task goes to state 255 and frees itself. All 28 uses are stack-mode with the 0xA5 handle on top. Brightness/fade reading is from the code, not run live.

name: msgbox_load_portrait
args: operand low16 = face resource id (CD directory words 3299..3480; e.g. 0xD7D = Frei, 0xD39 = a young man), message-box index in the second value/word (always 0); stack form pops id then box index; called by library func_031F
evidence: LIVE: scene 0x1B (Frei's first line) executes library func_0331(0x950, 0xD7D, 0x50) -> func_031F -> 'push 0; push 0xD7D; a8 (stack)' (breakpoint at the handler 0x80075BB0, frame 7055) and 'ab' for the voice; by frame 7225 the box 'Frei / Welcome to Valha...' is on screen with a 112x136 portrait of Frei (winged tiara) at the bottom left. The resource is SLZ type 2 with a tile table (w,h,16x16 tiles) and an 8bpp TIM - decoded and re-assembled it is the portrait. Handler allocates the pool task 0x80055000 (+0x28 = id, +0x2C = box index) which streams the resource and copies it into the box at +0x32C; the box renderer 0x8004E6F4 draws it with 0x8004E334 (textured quads) or 0x8004DFEC (rects). Library func_0331(L0 voice id or -1, L4 face id or -1, L8 wait frames) is the wrapper scenes use before almost every spoken line (3,300+ calls).

name: load_voice_clip
args: operand low16 = clip resource id (CD directory words 0x912..~0xBB8 = 2322..3000: SPU ADPCM clips, 4-39 sectors); 0 inline words; also called by library func_031F with the first argument of func_0331 and by text command 12
evidence: LIVE: scene 0x16 'ab 0x94F' executes at frame 7512 (handler 0x80070814); it calls 0x8005A74C(0x94F) (hit the same frame), which picks one of 4 round-robin slots ([0x8007FD85] & 3) and creates the task 0x8005A864: read the directory word into a malloc'd buffer (slot table 0x8007F208, 8 bytes per slot, flag byte +5 = 5), no sin/cos (the dossier's reading came from a different callee). At frame 7658, when the message box 'Valkyrie / How nostalgic...' is on screen, the box code (return address 0x8004D854) calls 0x8003E204(buffer 0x800FE9D0, 0x7F40, 2, 0): a twin of 0x8003E134 (the sfx starter) that scales the volume byte by ctx+0x3C3 instead of ctx+0x3C2 (two separate volume settings, presumably SE and voice) and calls 0x80019834 = start a sound sequence from the memory buffer (0x7F40 = volume 0x7F / pan 0x40, as in op 0xDE); from then on 0x8001A100 (sound-engine poll) is called every frame (the clip is playing). The box state machine (0x8004D7B8..0x8004DBD0) uses the box flag +0x338 bits 0x04000000 (voice pending) / 0x08000000 (voice playing). Resource 0x94F occupies 9 sectors (<= 18 KB, header 0x1C then ADPCM-looking data: at most about 1.5 s at 22 kHz). So: queue/preload a voice clip that the next message box plays; text command 12 (u16 cue) calls the same 0x8005A74C. Name change: start_cd_effect -> load_voice_clip. 'Voice' rests on association with message boxes, ADPCM size and Lenneth's line timing; the audio itself was not listened to.

name: spawn_hotspot_marker
args: inline 1 word: operand low16 = x, word0 = y (map position); 46 uses, one per hotspot scene
evidence: Handler 0x8006F1D0 creates the task 0x800582F8 (+0x40 = x, +0x42 = y) bound to the first template whose first halfword is 2. Each frame the task tests actor 0's bounding box (+0x94/+0x98 plus the sprite box from its resource) against the rectangle (x-16..x+16, y-64..y); when the player overlaps it sets ctx+0x398 |= 1 (the flag is cleared again when the player leaves), plays sfx 8 at the player and grows the marker sprite (size fields +0x4C/+0x4E up to 24/36); leaving shrinks it (state 4). Scripts place it right after the 'register_trigger_zone 0x101' hotspot definitions ('ac 0x152 0x174' etc.). So it is the visible interaction marker (icon + blip sound) of a hotspot; the exact icon was not looked at.

name: set_anim_loop
args: inline 2 words: operand low16 = actor resource id (same id as spawn_actor 0x85), word0 = animation index, word1 = 0 or 1
evidence: Handler 0x80077B10 finds the loaded actor resource whose id equals the operand (table [0x8007EFD8]/hw 0x8007EFDC, 8 bytes per resource) and writes resource[8 + idx*8 + 6] = value. That byte is the end-of-animation behaviour of the 8-byte animation record [u32 offset][u16 frame count][u8 flags][u8 next]: the animation player (0x80037FB4) reads it when the frame counter reaches the count: bit0 clear (value 0) = play once, hold the last frame and raise the 'ended' flag 0x08000000 (what op 0x70 waits for), bit0 set and bit1 clear (value 1) = restart at frame 0 (loop) and raise the same flag each cycle, bit2 = chain to the animation in byte +7. Scripts use it right after the matching spawn and before 'set_anim; wait_anim_end' (e.g. 'ae 0x271B 4 0; 71; 70; 76'). Read from code; not run live.

name: get_trigger_kind
args: no args; result in G[0] = byte ctx+0x20E
evidence: Handler 0x80070A00 returns the byte at ctx+0x20E, byte 2 of the per-call word ctx+0x20C that the engine writes before calling an actor/trigger script. Writers: actor-vs-actor overlap (caller 0x800306CC/0x800309B0, a2 = 0) -> 0x80045294 stores (this_actor | other<<24 | 0x1000 | 0x30000) = kind 3; the action-button interaction (caller 0x80044C30, a2 = 1) stores 0x40000 = kind 4; b4 callbacks store 0x60200|actor = 6; bf calls or in 0x70800 = 7. So af tells a script why it was run: 3 = touched, 4 = talked to / action button, 6 = b4 actor callback, 7 = bf call. Scripts compare it to 3/4 in per-frame actor functions. Mechanism read from code; the touch/talk wording is inferred from the two callers.

name: party_roster_state_op
args: operand byte0 = roster index (1-based, up to 25), byte1 = mode (0 set, 1 clear, 2 get); stack form pops index then mode; get result in G[0]
evidence: Handler 0x800708D4 operates on the 25-entry table of 236-byte records [0x8007F1E4] (new-game init 0x8003C80C..0x8003C820 loops i = 0..24 calling 0x8003C33C(i) on it; records hold stats, e.g. entry 0 = 1000, 15, 10...). Byte +217: 0 = absent, 1 = acquired, 2 = in an active slot (set by e1). Mode 0 stores 1 into it, mode 1 stores 0 and also clears any of the four active-slot bytes ctx+0x39C..0x39F equal to the index, mode 2 returns it. Library func_030A(index) = 'party member joins': it is called at chapter ends before the jump to the world map (scene 0x800) with indexes 2, 4, 6, 7, 9-11, 13, 14, 16-25 or a variable (index 3 is followed by index 4 and 'e1 0x301 0x402' in scene 0x1D), adds G0x68.b*300 to ctx+0xA4 (not for 3/4) and then runs b2(index, 0). Cutscenes use b2 idx,1 after 'e2; e1 0 0' to hide a member and restore with e3. So the table is the character/party roster, not map entries. 'Roster of 25 = Lenneth + einherjar' is an inference from the structure; names of the characters were not checked.

name: actor_jump
args: inline 2 words (stack 2 + actor): operand low16 = actor idx, word0 = vertical speed (2,3,4,8), word1 = horizontal speed (signed 8.8, e.g. +-0x400, 0, -0x328); 198 uses
evidence: Shared queue handler 0x80076964: [0x8007F25C]&8 (script mode) -> queued command type 11 (0x8003B3C0), else 0x8003B3F8(actor, s1, s2) immediately: clears actor flags 0x4000400|0x800, sets 0x8 (the airborne bit the player landing code clears again, see 0x77), +0xAC (vertical velocity) = -s1<<8, +0xE0 = 0, stores s2 as the horizontal speed in the render task, puts it in state 6 and starts an animation. Used after 71/74/76 for hops and knock-backs. The velocity writes and the airborne flag make 'jump / launch' safe; not run live (first use is scene 0x1D, later story).

name: bgm_set_track_levels_timed
args: inline 2 words (stack 4): operand low byte = channel, word0 byte0/byte1 = two level bytes (0x00,0x40 / 0x00,0x80 / 0x01,0x80 / 0x00,0xBE), word1 = frames; 110 uses
evidence: Handler calls 0x8005B314(chan, a, b, frames): 0x80013F2C(sound object [0x8007FD8C], chan, a, b) rewrites the per-part level bytes of that channel at 0x8002B6C4+chan*2+k for every part k flagged in the mask table 0x8002B6C0 (mode byte 1: 'a != 0' flag; mode byte 2: the value b / a), then creates/refreshes the task 0x8005B3B0, which after 'frames' ticks calls 0x80013F2C(.., chan, 0, 0) to restore. So it temporarily overrides two level bytes of one music part for N frames. Used 110x in cutscenes at fixed times ('ba 0x4000 0x120', 'ba 0 0 2' to clear). What the two bytes are (volume/pan/mute of layered tracks) is not established; the 'temporary override then restore' part is certain.

name: engine_set_param
args: operand low16 = sub-op 0..11; 1 inline word (stack: sub-op on top, then value) = value. Sub-ops listed in notes.md (0 battle BGM id, 1 second BGM id, 2/8/10/11/6 flag bits in ctx+0x398, 3 scene tileset package, 4/5/7 unused, 9 battle start mode)
evidence: Jump table 0x8007E0A4. Sub-op 3 (845 of 1,080 uses, 49 distinct ids 0x59E..0x5CE) is a package id: the preload task 0x80043C4C reads it, together with the fixed packages 1487 (0x5CF) and 1488/1489 (picked by a bit of the active character's item byte), into buffers kept at ctx+4/+0xC/+0x10. I decompressed 0x59E and 0x5C9: each is a 5-part package: a small table, an SLZ block that decompresses to MIPS code (jal targets 0x80081D8C, 0x80082368, 0x80060044, 0x80021C80, i.e. calls into the field engine), a ~200 KB 8bpp TIM (dark wood planks, bookshelves = interior tile textures) and a 4bpp TIM. So sub-op 3 selects the scene's tile graphics/map code module. Sub-op 0 holds a BGM directory word (script values 2249..2282 = the play_bgm id space; reset default 0x8C4): the loader preloads that file when it differs from ctx+0x38C (the id play_bgm last loaded); library func_09E7(battle, bgm, bgm2, flag) sets it (and sub 1) right before start_battle. Sub-op 9 ([0x8007FD89], values 1/3) is read inside start_battle (0x8004227C, 0x800423E8) and selects which of ctx+0x398 bits 4/8 are set (0 = decide from the situation, 2 -> 4, 3 -> 8). Sub-ops 2/8/10/11 (flag bits 2/0x100/0x1000/0x2000 of ctx+0x398) are written in clusters just before start_battle; no reader exists in the field engine, so the battle module reads them. Sub-op 6 (0x200, 156 uses, always 1) is set at scene start of dungeon scenes after 'play_bgm 0x8B3'. 4/5/7 have no uses.

name: actor_set_sort_params
args: operand low16 = actor id (0xFFFF = current actor); 1 inline word: low byte -> actor+0x102, next byte -> actor+0x103 (observed 0x3800, 0x3802, 0x1902, 0x6403, ...)
evidence: Handler 0x80070154 stores the two bytes. +0x102 is initialised from [0x8007FD46] at actor creation and its bit 0 selects the depth value in the actor draw routine 0x80038278: bit0 clear -> 0x80038154 result + 0x100, bit0 set -> the plain result (an ordering-table depth bias between the actor and the map layers); script values for +0x102 are 0, 2 or 3. +0x103 (the 0x19..0x64 byte, initialised from [0x8007FD44]) is written at 0x80036770 and 0x800701C4 and read nowhere in this overlay. Meaning of the second byte unknown; first byte = draw depth/priority bias is the best reading.

name: sound_seq_set_position
args: 4 stack values popped (top first): handle (from d3), x, y, volume; NEVER used in scene code
evidence: Handler 0x80070460 looks up the d3 task by handle (0x800702D4) and, if its sequence slot byte (+0xF) is not 0xFF, calls 0x800593EC(slot, x, y, volume, 0x2000) - the same routine op 0xD2 (update_sfx_position) uses for plain sfx voices, and the one the actor sfx task 0x8003B734 calls every frame to re-pan/re-attenuate from the map position relative to the camera. So it is the position update for a positional sound sequence started with d3/d4. Mechanism from code; never used.

name: set_battle_return_scene
args: operand low16 = scene id (index into the 10-byte table 0x80080618); 2 inline words: x | y<<16 arrival position, byte; ONE use (scene 0xEB)
evidence: Handler 0x8006FB44 writes ctx+0x318 = scene id, ctx+0x312 = table[id].dir word, ctx+0x314 = 0x8006B228(...), ctx+0x94/+0x98 = x/y, ctx+0x39B = byte (live values at Valhalla: ctx+0x318 = 0x16 = the current scene, +0x312 = 0xE30 = 3632 = 3610+0x16, +0x314 = 0xE16) and sets [0x8007F260] |= 0x2000. That flag is tested in start_battle 0x8004227C (0x800426A8): with it set ctx+0x39A = 4, ctx+0x38C (current BGM id) = -1 and ctx+0x24 = 0, else ctx+0x39A = 2. The single use (scene 0xEB, the sluice-gate/final area) is 'd8 0xEC (0x01A8013B, 0); func_09E7(battle 0x43B, bgm 0x8D2, ...); wait 60; select_scene 0xEC; change_scene 0x01A8013B' i.e. it stages the destination scene and arrival position before a scripted boss battle. Hypothesis, one use only.

name: sound_engine_latch_ctx_field
args: none; never used in scene code or the library
evidence: Handler 0x800709DC copies ctx+0x18 into the sound engine structure ([0x8007FD9C]+0x1C) and sets its byte +5 = 1. The BGM preload task does the same thing inline when ctx+0x38E (c9 sub-op 1) == -1 (0x800435D0..0x800435F8), so the pair looks like 'point the sound engine at the preloaded music data'. ctx+0x18 is a heap pointer (zero in the Valhalla snapshot). Dead built-in; purpose still a guess.

name: set_msgbox_portrait_flip
args: value in instruction low 16 bits (inline, always 0/1 in scripts) or 1 popped; nonzero = set, 0 = clear
evidence: Handler 0x80075C5C sets/clears bit 27 (0x08000000) of [0x8007F260]. 2,232 of its 4,499 uses are in library func_033C (message placement): anchor 0 and 3 -> 'e0 1', anchors 1 and 2 -> 'e0 0' right before 0x92/0x93/0x94 (anchors 8-15 pick 1/0 from the facing byte of that actor). The only reader in the field overlay is the text renderer 0x8004BF6C at 0x8004C860: when a line slot (box+0x4A6..) is armed with the mode value -1 it copies that bit into message-box flag bit 0 (box+0x338), otherwise it sets/clears bit 0 from the mode. Box flag bit 0 is tested at 0x8004E6F4 in the portrait drawing routine (the buffer at box+0x32C loaded by 0xA8): set = the portrait is built from textured quads (GPU 0x2C/0x2E, routine 0x8004E334, vertex x = width - tile x, i.e. mirrored), clear = plain sprite rectangles (0x64/0x66, routine 0x8004DFEC). LIVE (scene 0x1B patched into place, Frei's line 'Welcome to Valhalla', box flags +0x338 = 0x08220001 at 0x800FD0F0): (1) forcing the e0 argument 1 -> 0 at the call changed nothing (0 differing pixels 90 frames later); (2) clearing box bit 0 by hand changed nothing in 2 frames; (3) setting it again made Frei's portrait jump from the bottom-left to the bottom-right of the screen, mirrored. So bit 0 does control portrait mirroring/side, but e0's value at the start of the line did not change the picture, so when the renderer re-samples it (only when a slot is re-armed with mode -1) was not pinned down. Name changed from set_msgbox_flag: what it does to the portrait is medium confidence, the exact trigger is not understood.

name: set_character_item
args: character index (1-based): inline = ins low 16 bits, stack = top; value: 1 inline word or 2nd pop; -1 = query only; returns the previous value in G[0]
evidence: Handler 0x80070D2C: entry = [0x8007F1E4] + 236*(idx-1), i.e. the same 25-record roster table as b2/e1 (not the 264-byte actor table); G[0] = old halfword at entry+20, then (unless -1) stores the new value, looks it up in the 3-byte table [0x8007F204] (also used by e5/e6) and builds 3 'mode' slots at +157..159; for index 1 it also flips movement flag bits at +156. In the roster records the halfword at +20 is the first of a list of ids (e.g. 0x49 0xAA 0xB4 0xBE 0xC3), so it is more likely an equipped weapon/attack id than a generic item. 4 uses (scenes 0x6F, 0x3EC, 0x3EE): 'e4 5 0x61 ... push L0 ... e4' save/restore and 'e4 1 -1' compared with 0x100.

name: add_hud_gauge_0x388
args: signed 16-bit delta: inline = ins low 16 bits, or 1 popped; 0 inline words; NEVER used in scene code
evidence: Handler 0x80071044: ctx.halfword[0x388] += arg (no clamp). The only other code touching it is the HUD routine at 0x800601C8..0x80060244: +1 per frame (cap 100) while idle, -5 per frame (floor 0) while the other state is active, with a bar drawn at (58,32) by 0x80060948 in the same routine; the same routine adds G0x68.b*500+100 to G[0x20] (capped at 999,999,999) when it fires. A 0..100 recharge-style gauge; what it is called in game is unknown. Purely mechanical name.

name: reset_active_actor_motion
args: none (0 inline words)
evidence: Handler 0x8007109C loops over the 25 roster records [0x8007F1E4] (236 bytes each) and for those with role byte (+217) 1 or 2 clears halfword +214 and copies word +176 to +172 (the reset e3 does when its flag is nonzero). 3 uses (scenes 0x6E, 0x6F, 0x3EC), all at the end of a scripted walk: '... call func_09E7?; ea; c9 8 0; b2 0x103; e1 0 0; e3'. What +172/+176/+214 are (position / target / velocity of the follower) is not established.

name: add_ctx_counter_0xa4
args: 1 inline word (signed amount) or 1 popped
evidence: Handler 0x800710E8: ctx.word[0xA4] += arg. name: set_map_exploration_tracking
args: value = instruction low byte (always 0 in the 22 uses): 0 = tracking OFF (sets bit 9 of [0x8007F264]), nonzero = on; 0 inline words
evidence: Handler 0x8007115C sets (arg == 0) or clears bit 0x200 of halfword [0x8007F264]. Reader: the per-frame routine 0x80055AF4 returns at once when the bit is set, and when the scene-table entry (0x80080618 + id*10, field +2) is non-zero otherwise walks the map cells under the camera rectangle and sets bit (cell tile index + table field +4) in the bitset at ctx+0xAF2. New-game init (0x8003C798) clears exactly that area (0x498 = 1,176 bytes), and scene reset 0x8006D5F0 clears the flag. So ctx+0xAF2 is a per-cell 'visited' bitmap (dungeon auto-map); ec 0 switches the marking off for a room (22 uses, always at the top of a room's entry function: 'ec 0; 81 5; a1 ...'). The bitmap's consumer (map screen) was not located and nothing was run live.

name: get_interact_actor_res_id
args: no args (0 inline words); result in G[0]
evidence: Handler 0x80078F7C: if [0x8007F260] bit 1 or [0x8007F25C] bit 28 is set, G[0] = halfword +188 of the 264-byte actor entry indexed by the byte ctx[0xFFB]; else 0. Halfword +188 is the actor's resource/type id (a2 property 4: 'resource id'); ctx[0xFFB] and F260 bit 1 are set together by the action-button interaction code at 0x80044B54 (the same code that calls 0x8004528C with kind 4, see 0xAF).
